citation_policy: Each source supports only supported_claims. All morphology relations, confusion tests and adoption plans are researcher proposals unless separately marked. No cached ChatGPT citation token is a source.

sources.title: J.K. Rowling — Clothing
sources.supported_claims: Plain robes and optional pointed hats are the basic wizard dress; long dresses and formal occasions are described.
sources.claim_limits: Does not establish film shirts/ties, fixed robe opening, exact garment fibers or a universal wearer design.

sources.title: J.K. Rowling — Colours
sources.supported_claims: The four house palettes are red/gold, green/silver, yellow/black, blue/bronze.
sources.claim_limits: Colour associations and fictional values do not prove a wearer's personality, blood status or intelligence.

sources.title: How film characters compare to book descriptions
sources.supported_claims: Distinguishes Harry eye colour and scar placement, Hermione hair/teeth, Narcissa two-tone hair, Tonks coat and Kingsley costume inspiration.
sources.claim_limits: Confirms selected contrasts, not every seed-row detail. Exact regional hair placement depends on a particular image; costume inspiration is not inferred wearer nationality.

sources.title: Warner Bros. Studio Tour — Costumes
sources.supported_claims: Distinguishes early/later Quidditch kit, training gear, film pink silk/chiffon ball gown, French-blue uniform and epilogue accessories.
sources.claim_limits: Production materials concern documented costumes. Replica materials and generic silhouette descriptions are separate.

sources.title: Hogwarts haute couture
sources.supported_claims: Lists ball/wedding gown variants, Lockhart's duelling ensemble, matching blue capelets, monogram knits and Luna's three-dimensional party tiers.
sources.claim_limits: Fleur's two black birds are named phoenixes. Does not specify the exact sewing or applique process of that garment.

sources.title: Jany Temime costume designer interview
sources.supported_claims: The third-film uniform redesign added a hood, interior house-colour distinction, silk ties and changed knit/trouser/skirt construction.
sources.claim_limits: Wording mentions an interior collar; don't turn it into a universal lining specification for every film. Page metadata and URL dates differ.

sources.title: Designing deathly masks
sources.supported_claims: Contrasts fourth-film partial-face masks with fifth-film whole-face coverage, silvery ornament and coordinated garment embroidery.
sources.claim_limits: Coverage, material appearance and group variation are separate. A mask isn't a species face; engraved pattern isn't an open hole.

sources.title: Warner Bros. Studio Tour — Creature Effects
sources.supported_claims: Buckbeak was informed by eagle anatomy; goblin ears/noses/chins vary by individual; Aragog used individually inserted hair.
sources.claim_limits: Practical puppet materials do not establish fictional body materials or universal species measurements.

sources.title: Warner Bros. Studio Tour — press pack
sources.supported_claims: Documents makeup, animatronics, digital scanning and Voldemort's digitally replaced snake-like nose.
sources.claim_limits: Tracking dots, silicone, goat hair and stunt foam are production evidence, not appearance requirements or fictional anatomy.

sources.title: The Dark Mark — Encyclopedia
sources.supported_claims: Skull/serpent motif occurs as a forearm mark and a separate sky sign.
sources.claim_limits: A shared motif does not establish shared owner, surface, scale or embodiment; magic activation is not established by a static mark.

sources.title: Mad-Eye Moody's eye — Encyclopedia
sources.supported_claims: Describes an artificial eye with an electric-blue iris and magical rotation/vision.
sources.claim_limits: Rotation and see-through function require temporal/narrative evidence; a blue eye or spectacle lens alone is not a replacement eye.

sources.title: J.K. Rowling — Illness and Disability
sources.supported_claims: Explicitly identifies Moody's wooden leg and magical eye and lasting magical injuries.
sources.claim_limits: Do not infer actual disability, health, cause of injury or danger from a real person's visual appearance.

sources.title: Time-Turner — Encyclopedia
sources.supported_claims: A small hourglass can be worn around the neck.
sources.claim_limits: Time travel and rotation are not proved by a still image. No precise ring count or metal purity is specified here.

sources.title: The Noble Collection — Time-Turner replica
sources.supported_claims: The replica has a central working miniature hourglass and rotating inner rings.
sources.claim_limits: Replica provenance only; the page lists conflicting size/chain lengths, which are excluded from visual invariants.

sources.title: Dementor — Encyclopedia
sources.supported_claims: Hooded/cloaked gliding figure with grey scabbed skin.
sources.claim_limits: A still robe does not establish gliding, soul extraction, depression or a formerly living human ghost.

sources.title: Luna's eight wackiest moments
sources.supported_claims: Documents glasses, vegetable-like earrings and lion-hat examples.
sources.claim_limits: The glasses' alleged invisible-creature function and claims about personality are excluded from positive appearance text.

sources.title: Eddie Redmayne / Colleen Atwood on Newt's coat
sources.supported_claims: Coat is described as dark peacock/petrol blue; upper fit and short trouser length are discussed.
sources.claim_limits: Limits the observation to the first Fantastic Beasts version; not all later coats, exact fabric identity or mandatory body proportions.

sources.title: Colleen Atwood on Graves' costume
sources.supported_claims: Elongated coat, emphasized shoulders, cashmere/Lurex, graphic monochrome edging.
sources.claim_limits: Wet-looking shine is textile appearance; do not assert the coat is physically wet or made of latex.

sources.title: Dressing the Goldstein sisters
sources.supported_claims: Contrasts looser ordinary-cloth, muted-cool coats with lighter rosy costume direction; honey-colour bob mentioned.
sources.claim_limits: Does not independently verify Queenie's exact peach/pink coat gradient from the seed. Hold that precise placement.

sources.title: First Cursed Child Malfoy portraits
sources.supported_claims: 2016 cast portraits and Scorpius' blond hair/constraining school uniform are discussed.
sources.claim_limits: Cast/costume version remains attached to the case. Do not turn a portrait into a timeless canon description.

sources.title: Younger vs Cursed Child Draco
sources.supported_claims: Contrasts short school hair with a long adult ponytail.
sources.claim_limits: Long hair is not evidence of genderbend, a female identity or a transition event.

sources.title: Novelpia — 악역영애 말포이
sources.supported_claims: Listing attributes the work to 고속도루, names 카리나 말포이, and has dated 2021 notices.
sources.claim_limits: The synopsis does not fix hairstyle, eye colour, clothes or all fanart lineage. First publication date and every chapter were not audited.

sources.title: Know Your Meme — Female Draco
sources.supported_claims: Lists older and September-2026 artist posts and terminology.
sources.claim_limits: Used for discovery/context only. No population frequency, earliest global origin, causal lineage or stable engagement counts are established.

sources.title: REDTEN — original fanart
sources.supported_claims: Browser showed the 2026-09-22 KST post and its illustration: long light hair, green irises, dark hoops and house-inspired clothing.
sources.claim_limits: web.run returned 403; in-app browser directly displayed the media. One artist's example only; exact age and hair chemistry are unverified.

sources.title: masoq — original fanart
sources.supported_claims: Browser showed multiple drawings with long pale hair, green robe interior, grey knit/skirt and different poses; visible date 2026-09-30 KST.
sources.claim_limits: Secondary summaries use September 29 in a different timezone. No canonical eye colour, required skirt or global style frequency follows.

sources.title: Grizz — original fanart
sources.supported_claims: Browser showed the 2024-03-10 KST post and two long-hair, green/grey schoolwear variations, including dark nails and differing hair states.
sources.claim_limits: Evidence of a pre-2026 example, not the first genderbend ever. Illustrated age and identity are not established from pixels.

sources.title: V&A — Appliqué and embroidery glossary
sources.supported_claims: Defines fabric-on-fabric applique and separately describes couching/embroidery.
sources.claim_limits: Generic textile construction evidence only. Does not prove an observed movie motif used that manufacturing technique.

sources.title: The Met — Manus x Machina galleries
sources.supported_claims: Explains pleating, tailoring/soft dressmaking and distinct lace structures.
sources.claim_limits: Supports generic form boundaries; does not identify Fleur's specific pleat process or any fictional garment's fiber.

sources.title: The Met — Man and the Horse glossary
sources.supported_claims: Glossary defines jabot as cloth/lace hanging from a front collar.
sources.claim_limits: Only the indexed glossary excerpt was consulted; not a full PDF/image inspection. Does not fix fastening in a film.

sources.title: Bloomsbury Team — Hogwarts professors
sources.supported_claims: Includes half-moon glasses, long beard, tight bun/square glasses/green cloak, hooked nose/dark hair.
sources.claim_limits: Book summary; actor likeness and every film costume variant are separate.

sources.title: Fashionable Hogwarts teachers
sources.supported_claims: Includes Trelawney jewelry, Boggart clothing, human/equine hybrid and younger Dumbledore plum velvet tailoring.
sources.claim_limits: Contains an apparent source-book misattribution for the Firenze passage; exact book citation must be rechecked before canon integration.

sources.title: Augusta Longbottom
sources.supported_claims: Describes the Boggart's long green dress and stuffed-vulture hat.
sources.claim_limits: This is a Boggart imitating Snape, not proof Snape changed anatomical sex or wore the clothes in ordinary life.

sources.title: Ravenclaw House Tie — official shop
sources.supported_claims: The shop tie uses navy/silver.
sources.claim_limits: Merchandise supports this product colourway. Polyester content does not transfer to filmed silk ties; film-wide placement still needs a versioned still.

sources.title: Ravenclaw — official house page
sources.supported_claims: Lists blue/bronze and eagle.
sources.claim_limits: Distinguish canon summary, filmed crest, merchandise and adaptation versions.

sources.title: Designing Harry Potter wands
sources.supported_claims: Contrasts plain/curved/bone-like handles and resin/rubber duplicates.
sources.claim_limits: Prop fabrication is not biological bone; grip, cane extraction and pose need their own evidence.

sources.title: Dark magical objects
sources.supported_claims: Separates magical silver replacement hand, forearm-related punishment marks, masks and other objects.
sources.claim_limits: Injury, tattoo, glove and independent severed-hand object must not share activation or owner mapping.

sources.title: When magic goes wrong
sources.supported_claims: Confirms the failed cat transformation case.
sources.claim_limits: Does not independently confirm seed's grey film fur; species transformation and decorative cat ears remain distinct.

sources.title: Useful wizarding objects
sources.supported_claims: Mentions Hermione's magically extended beaded handbag.
sources.claim_limits: Capacity and magic do not follow from a single photograph of a small beaded pouch.

sources.title: Colour coordinating the wizarding world
sources.supported_claims: Describes progressively deeper pink in film Umbridge costumes.
sources.claim_limits: Increasing colour saturation is observable only in matched sequence/variants; 'authority' is a contextual interpretation.

sources.title: First and last character appearances
sources.supported_claims: Contrasts first-book pointed pale face with epilogue high-buttoned coat, receding hair and pointed chin.
sources.claim_limits: Book epilogue is different from film inherited ring/tie pin and stage ponytail.

sources.title: Costume distressing activity
sources.supported_claims: Studio educational source explicitly concerns costume distressing.
sources.claim_limits: Indexed title only; details remain an acquisition lead. Do not claim exact coat weathering chronology from it.

sources.title: Narcissa official promotional photograph
sources.supported_claims: Observed dark crown/front roll with lighter face-side/lower hair, and a long green patterned tailored coat.
sources.claim_limits: Single promotional front view at browser display scale; rear/root topology and fiber identity cannot be inferred. Not a generated-image qualification.

sources.title: Luna official Christmas-party still
sources.supported_claims: Observed three flared tier outlines on a short metallic-looking dress and a dangling star-like earring.
sources.claim_limits: Metallic appearance is not metal-fiber identification; one view cannot prove hidden seams. Not a new native render.

sources.title: The shrewd skills of Severus Snape
sources.supported_claims: Book excerpt explicitly distinguishes transparent ghosts, and editorial describes long black hair/robes.
sources.claim_limits: Transparency alone doesn't establish which formerly living person, a death story or ghost identity.

sources.title: Wizarding fashion icons: ranked
sources.supported_claims: Describes Rita's acid-green quill, book-like costume accessories, half-moon eyewear and the Boggart outfit.
sources.claim_limits: Rankings and personality commentary are excluded from retrieval; exact bag material and all clothing colours still need dedicated primary evidence.

sources.title: Every time Draco was too Draco
sources.supported_claims: Describes the hippogriff as an eagle/horse hybrid with talons, and a separate animal-transformation episode.
sources.claim_limits: Editorial speculation about Patronus/attitude isn't reliable anatomy; exact wing/leg proportions need creator/image evidence.
